The IKSN is 20 bytes and the right-most 4 bytes (Transaction Counter) must be initialized to 0's.

The initial value of a 20-byte IKSN must follow the format PPPPXXXXXXXXXXEZ0000.
In IKSN format, PPPP represents HEX characters (F's).
In IKSN format, XXXXXXXXXX represents any 10-byte HEX character string.
In IKSN format, E represents any even HEX character (e.g., 0, 2, C, E).
In IKSN format, Z represents zero.
In IKSN format, 0000 represents the Transaction Counter value.
The Transaction Counter can be manually included in the IKSN or programmatically concatenated by vendor software such as MKIXOR.

BUYPASS maintains two sets of daily totals for each merchant: shift totals and settlement totals.
Shift totals accumulate from work shift to work shift and are scratch totals that do not affect settlement.
Shift totals can accumulate beyond a merchant's cut time.
Shift totals requests can be read only or read and reset.
For a Read Only Total Request, enter Totals Date code 111111 in the device date field.
Totals Date code 111111 enables viewing shift totals without resetting shift total amounts to zero.

For a Read and Reset Total Request, enter Totals Date code 999999 in the device date field.
Totals Date code 999999 enables viewing shift totals and resetting shift total amounts to zero.
For Totals Date code 999999, BUYPASS ends the current shift and resets merchant shift totals to zero.
If shift totals are not requested at shift end, totals continue to accumulate until a 999999 request is made.
Shift totals are available until the first transaction in a new shift has been completed.
Shift totals can be retrieved from the most recently completed shift.
Settlement totals accumulate over a 24-hour period and are totaled once a day.
Settlement time (cut time) is determined by the merchant.
A merchant may cut totals before the default settlement time; such a merchant is a variable-cut merchant.
Settlement totals can be requested as read only or read and cut.
Business day totals can be requested as read only for current, previous, or the business day before the previous.
For read-only settlement totals, enter the desired settlement date in format MMDDYY in the device date field.
Using Totals Date code MMDDYY returns totals for transactions that settled on the specified date.
Read-only request with a specific date allows viewing totals without resetting BUYPASS settlement total amounts to zero.
Settlement date is when transactions actually settle; it may not coincide with BUYPASS end-of-business day.
In most cases, to retrieve totals for a current business day, request totals using settlement date equal to business day plus one day.
BUYPASS groups transactions done in the end-of-business 24-hour period and totals them, but does not run settlement until 2:00 p.m.
If merchant end-of-day is 6:00 p.m., transactions for that day settle at 2:00 p.m. on the following day.
Read and cut settlement totals request option can be used only by variable-cut merchants.
To request totals for the current settlement date as read and cut, enter Totals Date code 222222 in the device date field.
Entering 222222 allows a variable-cut merchant to close its business day before the predetermined cut time in the BUYPASS merchant profile.
If the merchant does not request read and cut totals, BUYPASS automatically closes the business day at the designated cut time.
Transactions performed after close of business are included in the next business day's totals.
In controller-based automated fuel pump environments, the controller should connect to BUYPASS 30 minutes before cut time and forward all queued trailer transactions.
Forwarding queued trailer transactions before cut time ensures authorization-only/preauthorization pairs are captured on the same business day.
After transmitting all trailer transactions, the controller completes a read and cut total request using Totals Date code 222222.

Calendar days may elapse between business days; e.g., a Monday request can return totals for the previous Thursday if no weekend transactions occurred.

Vendors who support their own applications do not use software update processing.
Software update processing uses an automated request by an active device for a full application download from BUYPASS-supported device management.
A bit is set on the merchant profile at BUYPASS indicating the device must request a DLL.
When the merchant profile bit indicates a DLL is required, BUYPASS sends Download Indicator = 1 in the next transaction response.
After receiving Download Indicator = 1, the device sends a Table Load request to BUYPASS.
In response to a Table Load request, BUYPASS sends Software Dial Load Data Segment and Software IP Load Data Segment.
Device stores New Software Version, Software Terminal Record ID, Software Load Phone Number or Software Load IP/URL Address, Software Load Request Date, and Software Load Request Time.
At the designated date and time, the device dials the Software Load Phone Number/Software Load IP/URL Address and requests a full application load.
Upon completion of the full application load, the device dials BUYPASS and requests a Table Load.
BUYPASS responds to the post-load Table Load request by sending the Table Load without requiring the merchant profile bit to be set.
The device can attempt to request the automated full application load a maximum of three times.
If the load request to Software Load Phone Number/Software Load IP/URL Address is unsuccessful, the device prints the "decline" message.

Payment token replaces the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number for device and/or e-commerce transactions.
Payment token issuance is performed by a token vault that generates and stores the payment token and associated PAN.
The operator of the token vault is referred to as the token service provider.
The token requestor is typically an acquirer, merchant, or digital wallet provider using tokens to replace PAN in databases and processing.
Payment processes needing token support may include authorization, capture, clearing, and exception processing.
For additional payment tokenization terminology information, refer to Appendix O (Payment Tokenization Terminologies).
Payment Token ranges will be in the existing ranges of the relevant card brand.
Payment Tokenization replaces the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number for device and/or eCommerce payment transactions.
Payment Tokens are mapped to the PAN, leveraging existing payments infrastructure and messaging formats for authorization and processing.
The Payment Token will be used for the entire life-cycle of the transaction for all card brands.
EMVCo manages the Payment Token Standard.
A payment token transaction replaces the actual card PAN with an association payment token.
Payment token transactions may occur for NFC transactions when the NFC device sends a Payment Token instead of the actual card number.
Payment token transactions may occur for eCommerce transactions with security data containing token cryptogram, like VPAS or UCAF.
Payment token transactions may occur for card-on-file where the initial transaction contains the token with valid cryptogram and may be saved for subsequent transactions.
For NFC in-person purchase, merchant submits authorization as a contactless transaction exactly as they do today.
For mobile app (in app) eCommerce, merchant sends authorization request with appropriate data including the cryptogram.
For Mobile App (In App) eCommerce subsequent token transactions, specific field requirements must be included in the authorization request to avoid decline.
Specific field requirements for subsequent token-transaction authorizations vary by card brand.
In Card On File (COF), the payment token provided by the card brand replaces the PAN stored at the merchant.
A stored credential includes an account number or payment token stored by merchant/agent/payment facilitator/staged digital wallet operator for future transactions.
A credential is not considered a stored credential when card details are stored to complete a single transaction.
A credential is not considered a stored credential when card details are stored to complete multiple authorizations related to the initial transaction (e.g., incremental transactions).
A Cardholder-Initiated Transaction (CIT) is any transaction where the cardholder actively participates, in-store, online checkout, or a subsequent stored credential transaction.
A Merchant-Initiated Transaction (MIT) is a subsequent transaction with already stored credentials without the cardholder’s active engagement, based on prior consent.
Once credentials are shared for storage at a merchant location/website, standing instruction MITs are considered subsequent transactions.
A separate transaction to buy a different item again using the same card at the same merchant location/website is considered a subsequent transaction (standing instruction MIT).
A recurring transaction associated with the original transaction is considered a subsequent transaction (standing instruction MIT).
An installment transaction associated with the original transaction is considered a subsequent transaction (standing instruction MIT).
